title: Lodestar: An Online-Learning LLM Inference Router
technique: online-learned MLP reward predictor (reward = -TTFT) over per-request cluster-state and request features; route each request to argmax predicted reward

optimized_metrics.evidence: We use −TTFT as the main reward in this paper
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: We use −TTFT as the main reward in this paper

headline_claim.text: Lodestar achieves 1.41× lower average TTFT and 1.47× lower P99 TTFT on average (up to 2.15×/1.86× on homogeneous and 4.38×/4.42× on heterogeneous clusters) compared to a state-of-the-art prefix cache and load-aware heuristic

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We define the reward as the negative of observed TTFT, y_imax = −TTFT_imax, where imax is the selected instance index.
metric_definitions.notes: per-request scalar reward; TTFT in seconds (footnote 7)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: all input tokens in parallel and emits the first output token
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT is never given a formal definition; queueing is implicitly included since 'requests (queueing delay)' is a routing feature and TTFT is the observed latency at the client/gateway

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Lodestar optimizes time-to-first-token (TTFT) latency for two reasons: TTFT is critical to the user experience, and Time-per-output-token (TPOT) or end-to-end latency is not the right metric to optimize. The time that TPOT and end-to-end latency are observed is much further in the future than the routing decision time. Additionally, they are affected by one more unknown factor, the number of decode tokens, becoming even a more noisy signal.
metric_definitions.notes: explicit justification for choosing TTFT as reward; credit-assignment delay and decode-length noise

load_regime: request-rate sweep (RPS fixed per run, e.g. ToolAgent RPS 12/22, Conversation RPS 21) over Mooncake trace workloads; also prefix-sharing-ratio sweeps and workload shifts for online adaptation
tradeoff_acknowledged: Prefix-cache locality vs load balance is the tension in routing (fixed heuristic thresholds are workload dependent); learned policy adds routing overhead on the critical path (measured Fig 12). No explicit metric trade-off.
hardware: public-cloud K8s: 8x NVIDIA A30 (homogeneous); 8 A30 + 8 V100 (heterogeneous); L20 cluster for motivation
models: Llama3 8B (FP16, vLLM v1, chunked prefill); DeepSeek 7B in motivation
workloads: Mooncake conversation, toolagent, synthetic; prefix-sharing ratio workloads
extractor_notes: Objective is per-request TTFT (mean-reward learning); P99 is only a reported outcome, though ablation notes consistent-hashing filter 'damps tail TTFT'. TTFT, P99 never formally defined. TPOT/E2E explicitly rejected as the reward. No SLO/goodput. Baseline set: Least-request, Prefix-cache(τ), Prefix-cache-and-load-aware (AIBrix), Mooncake simulator-based. | TAIL AUDIT 2026-10-06: demoted TTFT@P99 (non-tail entry kept)

tail_audit.correction: Remove TTFT P99 'objective'; keep mean TTFT objective. P99 is headline-only.
